note: A plus el becomes al. It also goes before a person as the object: Veo a Juan.
De plus el becomes del.

ex.es: Las llaves están en la mesa.
ex.en: The keys are on the table.

note: With mí and ti it becomes conmigo and contigo.

ex.en: I take my coffee without sugar.

en: for, in order to, by a deadline
note: For purpose, recipient, destination and deadlines. See the por vs. para guide.
For cause, exchange, duration and movement through a place. See the por vs. para guide.

ex.es: La farmacia está entre el banco y la iglesia.
ex.en: The pharmacy is between the bank and the church.

en: until, up to, as far as

ex.es: Según mi madre, va a llover.
ex.en: According to my mother, it's going to rain.

ex.es: El abogado habló ante el juez.
ex.en: The lawyer spoke before the judge.

ex.es: Tras la tormenta, salió el sol.
ex.en: After the storm, the sun came out.

ex.es: Resolvieron el problema mediante el diálogo.
ex.en: They solved the problem through dialogue.

ex.es: Trabajo todos los días excepto el domingo.
ex.en: I work every day except Sunday.

ex.es: Lávate las manos antes de comer.
La finca está lejos de la ciudad.
ex.en: The farm is far from the city.

ex.es: Mi casa está al lado de la escuela.
ex.en: My house is next to the school.

ex.es: Se sentó junto a la ventana.
ex.en: She sat next to the window.

ex.es: Hay árboles alrededor de la casa.
ex.en: There are trees around the house.

ex.es: El gato está debajo de la cama.
ex.en: The cat is under the bed.

ex.es: Deja la caja encima de la mesa.
ex.en: Leave the box on top of the table.

ex.es: El taxi paró delante de la casa.
ex.en: The taxi stopped in front of the house.

ex.es: El patio está detrás de la cocina.
ex.en: The yard is behind the kitchen.
I'll be back within an hour.

en: across from, in front of, opposite

ex.es: La tienda está enfrente de la iglesia.
ex.en: The store is across from the church.

ex.es: El hotel está frente a la playa.
Lo supe a través de una amiga.
ex.en: I found out through a friend.

ex.es: Caminamos a lo largo de la playa.
Cerraron la escuela a causa de la tormenta.
ex.en: They closed the school because of the storm.

ex.es: El vuelo salió tarde debido a la lluvia.
ex.en: The flight left late due to the rain.

ex.es: Gracias a mi tía, conseguí trabajo.
ex.en: Thanks to my aunt, I got a job.

ex.es: Salimos a pesar de la lluvia.
ex.en: We went out despite the rain.

ex.es: Toma agua en vez de refresco.
Fui yo en lugar de mi hermana.
ex.en: I went in place of my sister.

ex.es: Votó en contra de la ley.
A partir de mañana, abrimos a las ocho.
ex.en: Starting tomorrow, we open at eight.

ex.es: Te traigo esto de parte de mi madre.
ex.en: I'm bringing you this from my mother.

note: Becomes e before a word starting with an i sound: padres e hijos.

ex.es: Mis padres e hijos viven aquí.
ex.en: My parents and children live here.
Do you want coffee or tea?

note: Becomes u before a word starting with an o sound: siete u ocho.

ex.en: I have seven or eight cousins.

note: Corrects a negative statement. Use pero everywhere else.

ex.en: I have neither a car nor a bike.

note: Also used in pairs: ni tú ni yo.

en: that, which, who (not in a question)

ex.en: I think it's going to rain.

note: Can't be dropped the way English drops that. Qué with an accent asks a question.

ex.en: I didn't go because I was sick.

note: One word, no accent. Por qué, as two words with an accent, asks why.

ex.en: Well, I don't know what to tell you.

ex.es: Como llovía, nos quedamos en casa.
ex.en: Since it was raining, we stayed home.

note: Cómo with an accent asks how.

ex.en: I'll call you when I get there.

note: Takes the subjunctive when talking about the future. Cuándo with an accent asks when.

ex.es: Esa es la casa donde nací.
ex.en: That's the house where I was born.

note: Dónde with an accent asks where.

ex.en: If it rains, we won't go out.

note: Sí with an accent means yes.

ex.en: I'm going even if it rains.

note: Subjunctive for even if, indicative for although.

ex.en: I listen to music while I cook.

ex.es: Yo cocino, mientras que él limpia.
Puesto que no vino, empezamos sin él.
ex.en: Since he didn't come, we started without him.

ex.es: Hablé claro, de modo que todos entendieron.
ex.en: I spoke clearly, so everyone understood.

ex.es: Te lo explico para que entiendas.
ex.en: I'll explain it so that you understand.

note: Always takes the subjunctive.

ex.es: Voy a la playa a menos que llueva.
ex.en: I'm going to the beach unless it rains.

note: Always takes the subjunctive.

ex.es: Te lo presto con tal de que me lo devuelvas.
ex.en: I'll lend it to you as long as you give it back.

note: Always takes the subjunctive.

ex.es: Salió sin que nadie lo viera.
ex.en: He left without anyone seeing him.

note: Always takes the subjunctive.
Always takes the subjunctive.

ex.es: Espera hasta que llegue tu padre.
ex.en: Wait until your father gets here.

ex.es: Vivo sola desde que murió mi esposo.
ex.en: I've lived alone since my husband died.
I'll let you know as soon as I arrive.

ex.es: Te llamo tan pronto como pueda.
ex.en: I'll call you as soon as I can.

ex.es: Llega a las ocho, o sea, en una hora.
ex.en: She arrives at eight, in other words, in an hour.

ex.es: Son mis suegros, es decir, los padres de mi esposa.
ex.en: They're my in-laws, that is, my wife's parents.

ex.es: Estudió mucho; sin embargo, no aprobó.
ex.en: He studied a lot; however, he didn't pass.

ex.es: No hay luz, por lo tanto, no hay clases.
ex.en: There's no power, therefore there are no classes.

note: Usually dropped, because the verb already shows the person. Keep it for emphasis.

ex.en: Are you coming to the party?

note: Tu without an accent means your.
Replaces tú in Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and parts of Central America and Colombia.
Takes the él form of the verb.
El without an accent means the.
Used for every group in Latin America, formal or not. Takes the ellos form of the verb.
Used for mixed groups too.

ex.es: Mi madre me llama cada día.
ex.en: My mother calls me every day.

ex.es: Lo vi ayer en el mercado.
ex.en: I saw him at the market yesterday.

en: to him, to her, to you (formal)
note: Becomes se before lo or la: se lo di.

ex.en: They invited us to the wedding.
I saw them at the beach.

note: Becomes se before lo or la: se lo dije.
Also makes general statements: aquí se habla español.
Mi without an accent means my.

ex.en: I think about you a lot.
I want to talk with you.
He always carries his passport with him.

note: Tú with an accent means you.

ex.es: Este carro es de mi tío.

ex.en: That building over there is new.

note: For things far from both people.
For something unnamed. It never changes form.
For something unnamed. It never changes form.

en: that thing over there, that (unnamed thing)

ex.en: What's that up in the sky?

note: After the verb it needs no first: no vino nadie.

ex.en: Do you want something to drink?

note: Spanish double negatives are correct.

ex.en: Do any of you speak English?

note: Shortens to algún before a masculine noun.
Shortens to ningún before a masculine noun.
Shortens to cualquier before a noun.
todas

ex.en: Each one pays their own share.

ex.es: Ella es la mujer con quien hablé.
ex.en: She's the woman I spoke with.

note: Quién with an accent asks who.

ex.en: I don't understand what you're saying.

en: the one who, the one that

ex.en: The one who arrives first wins.

forms: la que, los que, las que

ex.es: Llegó tarde, lo cual me molestó.
ex.en: He arrived late, which annoyed me.

ex.es: Es el hombre cuyo perro se perdió.
ex.en: He's the man whose dog got lost.

note: Agrees with the thing owned, not the owner.

ex.en: What do you want to eat?

note: Question words always carry an accent, even inside a sentence: no sé qué quiere.
Use it before es when asking for one item out of many.

ex.en: How many siblings do you have?

note: Two words with an accent. The answer uses porque.

ex.en: What do you need the money for?
What time does the train leave?
How long have you lived here?
How often do you go to the doctor?

ex.es: El mercado abre a las siete.

note: La, los and las are its other forms. A feminine noun starting with a stressed a takes el: el agua.

ex.es: Tengo un perro y una gata.
ex.en: I have a dog and a cat.

note: Unos and unas mean some: unos amigos.

ex.es: Vamos al parque después de clase.
ex.en: We're going to the park after class.

note: A plus el always joins into al. A la, a los and a las don't join.
De plus el always joins into del. De la, de los and de las don't join.

ex.en: I go to the gym every morning.

ex.es: Yo lavo los platos y los demás limpian la cocina.
ex.en: I wash the dishes and the others clean the kitchen.

note: Usually with los or las: los demás, las demás.

ex.en: I never saw such a thing.

note: Tal vez means maybe, and qué tal asks how something is.

ex.es: Comí tanto que no puedo moverme.
ex.en: I ate so much that I can't move.

note: Tantos and tantas mean so many: tantas personas.

ex.en: I have several cousins in Lima.

ex.es: La clase empieza a las tres.

ex.en: There are four of us in my family.
I work eight hours a day.
My nephew is nine years old.

ex.es: El museo abre a las diez.
Hay once jugadores en el equipo.
ex.en: There are eleven players on the team.
I live on the fourteenth floor.

ex.es: El autobús llega en quince minutos.
ex.en: The bus arrives in fifteen minutes.

ex.es: Hay diecisiete estudiantes en la clase.
ex.en: There are seventeen students in the class.

ex.es: A los dieciocho años puedes votar.
Mi hermana cumple diecinueve años mañana.
La casa tiene ochenta metros cuadrados.
ex.en: The house is eighty square meters.

ex.es: Hay cien personas en la fiesta.
ex.en: There are a hundred people at the party.

note: Ciento before another number: ciento veinte.

ex.en: The ticket costs a thousand pesos.

note: Miles means thousands: miles de personas.
